title: Substituting into formulae
subtitle: One formula, many values. Swap the letter for its number, then calculate.

explanation.title: One rule, used again and again
paragraphs: A cinema ticket costs £5, plus £2 for each snack. One friend wants 2 snacks. Another wants 4. Do you need a new price rule for each friend?
No. One rule covers everyone: C = 5 + 2s. This rule is a formula. The letter s stands for the number of snacks.
A letter in a formula is a placeholder. It holds a space for a number.
When you know the number, you swap the letter for it. This swap is called substitution.
After the swap, no letters are left. The formula has become a calculation. For s = 4, C = 5 + 2s becomes C = 5 + 2 × 4.
key_points: A number next to a letter means multiply: 2s means 2 × s.
Replace every copy of the letter.
Keep powers and brackets exactly where they are.
Put a negative value inside brackets.

steps.title: Find
steps.text: Write down each letter and the value you are given for it.

steps.title: Replace
steps.text: Rewrite the formula with every letter swapped for its value. Write × where a number meets a letter. Put brackets around any negative value.

steps.title: Calculate
steps.text: Work through it using BIDMAS: powers first, then multiply and divide, then add and subtract. Show one line of working at a time.

steps.title: Check
steps.text: Confirm every letter is gone. Add the unit to your answer if the question uses one.

interactive.title: Use the method
interactive.intro: Substitute s = 4 into C = 5 + 2s. Each step asks for one decision. A wrong choice tells you why it is wrong.

question_bank.title: Practise substitution
question_bank.intro: The questions get harder as you go: one letter first, then two letters, repeated letters, powers, brackets, negative values and division.
